title: Monomial generators and relations for an ideal tensor
statement: Let $Q$ be a commutative monoid, $K\subseteq Q$ satisfy $KQ\subseteq K$, $R=\mathbf Z[Q]$, $I=(z^q:q\in K)\subseteq R$, $A$ a commutative ring and $e:R\to A$ a ring map. Write $m_q\in I$ for $z^q$. Use the coefficient-first tensor $T=A\otimes_R I$ of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with scalar structure specified by $e$. Then $a\otimes m_{qr}=e(z^r)a\otimes m_q$. Additive maps from $T$ to any abelian group agree if they agree on all $a\otimes m_q$ for $q\in K,a\in A$. For every $A$-module $N$ and family $b:K\to N$ satisfying $b(qr)=e(z^r)b(q)$ for all $q\in K,r\in Q$, there is a unique $A$-linear map $f:T\to N$ with $f(a\otimes m_q)=ab(q)$. The empty ideal and arbitrary noncancellative monoids are allowed.

source.place: Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product; finite monomial calculation in ILO Expose VI 3.7(a), printed p. 75, and VIII 3.4.3, printed p. 110. Agent-written generators-and-relations proof.

proof.text: The support criterion MonoidAlgebra.mem_ideal_span_of_image says that each index in the support of an element of I is a multiple of an element of K. Closure KQ subset K makes this precisely support in K. Conversely a finite sum supported on K belongs to I. Thus the underlying integer module of I is the supported submodule, and supportedEquivFinsupp gives a basis indexed by K. Its basis element at q is m_q. This also proves the assertion when K is empty.

Extend b by integer linearity on this basis to l:I to N. For a monomial z^r, compare the integer linear maps x maps to l(z^r x) and x maps to e(z^r)l(x). On the basis vector m_q the hypothesis on b proves equality, since z^r m_q=m_{qr}. Integer linearity in the ring argument extends this equality to every r in R. Hence l is R-linear for the action induced by e.

The bilinear map (a,x) maps to a l(x) is balanced, so the universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], implemented by LinearMap.liftBaseChange, yields f. Its formula on monomials is the required one. Balancing also gives a tensor m_{qr}=e(z^r)a tensor m_q.

For uniqueness of arbitrary additive maps, first induct on tensors using generation by pure tensors from [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For a pure tensor a tensor x, induct on the ideal-span expression for x. The generators are the stated monomial tensors. Addition is preserved, zero is preserved, and a tensor (r x) equals (e(r)a) tensor x. This establishes equality on every tensor and in particular uniqueness of the linear lift.

theorem exists_lift (hK : ∀ q ∈ K, ∀ r : Q, q * r ∈ K)
    {N : Type t} [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
    (b : K → N)
    (hb : ∀ (q : Q) (hq : q ∈ K) (r : Q),
      b ⟨q * r, hK q hq r⟩ = e (MonoidAlgebra.of ℤ Q r) • b ⟨q, hq⟩) :
    letI := e.toAlgebra
    ∃ f : A ⊗[MonoidAlgebra ℤ Q] I →ₗ[A] N,
      ∀ (q : Q) (hq : q ∈ K) (a : A),
        f (a ⊗ₜ monomial K I hI q hq) = a • b ⟨q, hq⟩
